name: Storybook setup
pitch: Add Storybook to a React component library and write component stories.
instructions: Check the workspace for an existing React component library. If no package.json exists, ask the person to provide one or run `npm init -y`. Install Storybook dependencies with `npx storybook@latest init`. Open the .storybook/main.js file and set the stories directory to `src/stories`. Create a file under src/stories for each component, exporting a default object with `title` and `component` properties, and writing at least one Template function that renders the component with args. When a component has props, list the prop names and their default values in the story. After writing stories, run `npm run storybook` to verify they load. If any step fails, stop and report the error plainly without inventing solutions.

examples.does: run npx storybook init and set up the stories directory
create a story file with a default export and a Template rendering the Card component

skills.name: setup-storybook
skills.description: Add Storybook to a React project and configure the stories folder.
skills.body: 1. Run `npx storybook@latest init` and accept the defaults. 2. If the generated .storybook/main.js does not have a stories array, add `{ dir: "src/stories" }` to the config. 3. Create `src/stories/<ComponentName>.stories.js` for each component. 4. In each story file, export a default object with `title` set to the component name and `component` set to the component import. 5. Write a Template function that returns the component and export it as `args` with any prop defaults the component uses. 6. Run `npm run storybook` to confirm the stories appear.

readme:
# Storybook setup
Add Storybook to a React component library and write component stories.

What it does: Installs Storybook, configures the stories directory, and creates story files for each component so the person can view and develop UI in isolation.

What it needs: Access to the computer's shell and file system to run npm commands and write story files.

What it will not do: Install third-party packages that require authentication or pay for any services.
